The past corresponds to Series II, which is ergative.

Agentive subjects are marked in Series II. Agentivity does not by itself trigger ergative marking, however; see for example Series III (Hewitt 1995:338).

Non-agentive A takes ergative marking in Series II. Hewitt (1995, pp.187-189) provides multiple examples of inanimate/abstract agents with no volitional control taking the ergative case: sun-ERG (dried the field), sweat-ERG (penetrated the shirt), pleasure-ERG (made me dizzy), God-ERG (let you grow old), illness-ERG (weakened the man’s knees). These are Series II constructions and therefore take the ergative.
